######################################################################
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.chart-avoid | done
TITLE: Chart-avoid: ANSWERED — NO. The Z(diamond) chart does not confine its divisors; the binding constraint is FinCoverData
ANSWERED 2026-07-25 (run 0048 round 1). The answer is NO, on three independent grounds, and
nothing downstream is blocked on a human any more. Deliverable of record: informal/spec-dd-r.md
ADDENDUM 3, which supersedes ADDENDUM 2 §4 and ADDENDUM 1 item 2. Inbox I-0333 is answered.

(a) THE SEED CARRIES NO EXACTNESS DATUM. ThetaGeneratorSeed (Picard/DivSchemeFamily.lean:74)
has five fields, IsGenerator (:129) two; none mentions Theta, pole order or a chart. Every
universal instantiation of `side` picks an ARBITRARY chart containing the point (seedUniv
DivSchemeSeedUnivGen.lean:283, seedUniv' DivSchemeRedesignSeedUniv.lean:180, pointwiseSide
DivSchemeSeedUnivPointwise.lean:88), so a point of pi^-1(infinity) is legal everywhere.

(b) ADDENDUM 2 §4's "tractable half" IS A WHOLE DISJUNCT, AND ITS ARGUMENT IS CIRCULAR. Theta =
fiberWeilDivisor pi is supported on V_0 \ V_1 (FLVFiberToolkit.lean:292/:311/:254), so
set-theoretically Theta = V_1^c and "supportLocus cap pi^-1(infinity) = empty" IS the disjunct
supportLocus subset V_1. And IsGenerator.dvd makes supportLocus the base locus of K, so "a
generator of exact pole order a exists at y in Theta" holds iff the base locus misses y:
premise = conclusion.

(c) EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE, STABLE UNDER EVERY ZARISKI SHRINK. Over k[t] with C = P^1, pi = id,
F = t X^2 + X Y + t Y^2 cuts a relative effective Cartier divisor, finite flat of degree 2
(coefficients (t,1,t) generate the unit ideal). F(1,0) = F(0,1) = t, so the fibre at t = 0 is
Z(XY) = {0, infinity}: it meets BOTH vertical fibres. In the chart Y = 1, F = t(x^2+1) + x is
degree 1 in t with coprime coefficients, hence irreducible in k[x,t]; the only point over Y = 0
is (infinity, 0), in the closure. So D is IRREDUCIBLE, D -> A^1_t is finite surjective, and over
EVERY nonempty open of the base D stays irreducible hence preconnected. Every Zariski cover has
a member containing t = 0. By supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified this divisor is NOT
IsLocallyCertified.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: the witness this leaf previously cited, Spec R[x]/(x^2 - t) over k[t],
does NOT meet pi^-1(infinity) (its points x = +-sqrt t are always finite), so it is chart-confined
and is not a witness. The conclusion stands; the witness above is the correct one.

(d) THE OBSTRUCTION SURVIVES THE DivEq QUOTIENT (landed this round, kernel-checked,
Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean): DivEq.supportLocus_eq — the support locus is a divisor
invariant — hence not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses: NO representative of
the class admits a certified adaptation. DivFamZar is a DivEq quotient, so DivFamZar is not the
relative-divisor functor and divRep against it would represent the wrong object.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT is FinCoverData (DivisorFamily.lean:160-176), which hardwires
h_0 : Fin m_0 -> Gamma(V_0), h_1 : Fin m_1 -> Gamma(V_1) with a partition of unity on EACH pinned
chart. Not pi, not the cover's fineness, not the submodule L, not the base. Any repair must
introduce an adaptation piece NOT contained in a single pinned chart. Successor leaves: p1-aut,
fibre-avoid, cert-relocalize, confine-open.

######################################################################
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.fibre-avoid | pending
TITLE: Fibre-avoid: every relative divisor avoids two k-points of P^1 Zariski-locally on the base
THE COVERING OBLIGATION — what makes the atlas carve legitimate rather than lossy
(spec-dd-r ADDENDUM 3 §5). With p1-aut, this closes the certificate lane's geometric gate.

STATEMENT. For a relative divisor whose support is finite over Spec R, and any s in Spec R: the
fibre D_s is finite, so pi(D_s) is a finite subset of P^1 over kappa(s); if k is INFINITE then
P^1(k) is infinite, so two distinct c_0, c_1 in P^1(k) avoid pi(D_s). relCurve C R -> Spec R is
proper (instIsProperRelCurveHom, SupportTube.lean:194) hence closed, so the image of
supportLocus cap pi^-1({c_0,c_1}) is closed and misses s. Over the open complement the divisor is
confined to pi^-1(P^1 \ {c_0,c_1}) = V_0 inf V_1 for the gamma-twist carrying {c_0,c_1} to
{0,infinity}.

PAYOFF, ALREADY LANDED: chartPairCoverData / ofChartPair and
forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean) then give
clause (c1) FREE — no fibre, no tube, no packet idempotent. The base-open spread it needs is
confine-open's exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter.

TWO HYPOTHESES TO WATCH, both real risks, neither to be assumed silently:
 (i) k INFINITE. Challenge.lean states the Jacobian over an arbitrary field. A finite-field route
     needs |P^1(k)| > deg D, i.e. a base change to k(T) or a degree-d point; schedule it, do not
     assume it.
 (ii) FINITENESS OF THE SUPPORT OVER THE BASE must come from the seed's own degree data, NOT from
     the certificate — otherwise the argument is circular. This is the one genuinely load-bearing
     input of this leaf.

######################################################################
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.field-size | blocked
TITLE: Field-size: over a small finite field, what is DivFamZar? — the one remaining human decision
THE ONE QUESTION THAT STILL NEEDS A HUMAN (2026-07-25, run 0048 r1). It is NOT "does the
Z(diamond) chart confine its divisors" — that is answered, NO (see chart-avoid). It is:

  OVER A SMALL FINITE FIELD, WHERE |P^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2, WHAT IS DivFamZar SUPPOSED TO BE?

WHY THE QUESTION IS FORCED. Certifiability requires the support to sit inside the preimages of a
pinned PAIR of points of P^1 (chart-avoid + confine-open). Every repair therefore needs, at every
base point, two k-rational points of P^1 off pi(supp_s) — i.e. q + 1 >= n + 2. And the
counterexample that kills chart-avoidance is FIELD-INDEPENDENT: F = s X_0^2 + X_0 X_1 + s X_1^2
is irreducible over F_2 exactly as over Q, because s(x^2+1) + x is degree 1 in s with coprime
coefficients over any field. So enlarging the field is not an escape and small fields are a real
hole, not a footnote.

WHAT MAKES IT A HUMAN DECISION. Challenge.lean:96-99 states the Jacobian over an ARBITRARY field,
and there is no hypothesis on k stronger than [Field k] anywhere in Picard/ or RiemannRoch/ (510
occurrences of Field k; zero Infinite / IsAlgClosed / PerfectField). The three options are not
comparable on mathematical grounds alone:
 (a) accept |P^1(k)| >= n + 2 as a hypothesis, and RECORD that Challenge.lean:96-99 is then
     unreachable for small q — i.e. the challenge as stated is not solved;
 (b) plan a descent lane: divQProj (Picard/DivSchemeQProj.lean) is the right lever for fpqc
     descent from k'/k, so the Jacobian over k is obtained by descending from a big enough k';
 (c) generalize the pinned charts from k-rational points to closed points of degree d >= 2. This
     costs the two facts the whole design rests on — Gamma(P1 k, chartOpen k i) iso Polynomial k
     (Curve/P1Charts.lean:234,239) and isPrincipalIdealRing_chartSections (Curve/P1Points.lean:64)
     — because Cl(P^1 minus a degree-d point) = Z/d, not 0.

SETTLE THIS BEFORE p1-aut. It decides whether building the GL_2(k) action on P^1 is worth doing
at all: under (b) or (c) the twist may be unnecessary or insufficient.

######################################################################
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.joint-cover | rejected
TITLE: Relax FinCoverData's chart-wise partitions to a joint covering (I-0346's cheaper option)
REJECTED 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 2), on a source fact, before any Lean was written.

I-0346 recorded a cheaper untried repair than R1/PGL_2: "relaxing just the chart-wise
partitions of unity in FinCoverData to a JOINT covering drops the requirement from two
avoided points to ONE.  Worth trying before anyone builds PGL_2."

IT BUYS NOTHING, and the reason is a typing fact, not a proof attempt.  FinCoverData
(Picard/DivisorFamily.lean:160-176) types its pieces INTO the charts:
  h0 : Fin m0 -> Gamma(relCurve, V0)      (:166)
  h1 : Fin m1 -> Gamma(relCurve, V1)      (:168)
  pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen . h0) (basicOpen . h1)   (:186)
so every piece is a basic open OF ONE OF THE TWO PINNED CHARTS by construction, whatever
the partition data says.  Per-piece swallow-or-miss already holds for ANY cover by opens
(DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98 uses only openness of pieces), so a connected divisor still
lands in one piece, and basicOpen_le puts that piece inside one chart.  The joint-covering
relaxation changes the partition FIELDS; it cannot change where the pieces live.

SHARP FORM, which is what should be quoted from now on: no repair that keeps the pieces
inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P^1 can work.  Any real repair must
either vary the pinned pair (leaf p1-aut, the R1 route) or generalize FinCoverData's piece
TYPE away from the two charts (the recorded R2 alternative).

Cost of a rebuild if anyone tries it anyway: partition0/partition1 have ~31 grep hits over
10 files, and thetaIdealDatum copies them into BasicOpenCocycleDatum
(DivisorThetaDatum.lean:397-401), which needs chart-ring Ideal.span_range = top
(GluedSheafEngine.lean:84-92) for Serre vanishing.  It is a 10-file refactor for zero
mathematical gain.

######################################################################
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.p1-aut | pending
TITLE: P1-aut: the GL_2(k) action on P^1 — the one missing input of repair R1
THE COST OF REPAIR R1 (spec-dd-r ADDENDUM 3 §3). Every declaration in the DD-R chain is generic
in pi, constrained only by [IsFinite pi] / [IsAffineHom pi] (+ [IsDominant pi]) and
hpi : pi >> P1.structureMap k = C.left -> Spec k (DivSchemeSeedUnivFields.lean:58). So replacing
pi by gamma . pi for gamma in Aut(P^1_k) costs NOTHING in the landed material: every lemma
applies verbatim to the twisted map, and the twisted charts pi^-1(P^1 \ {c}) are affine because
pi is affine.

WHAT IS MISSING: Aut(P^1) does not exist in this project. P1 k is a Proj (Curve/P1.lean:135)
with chartOpen : Fin 2 -> Opens (:200); a workspace-wide search finds no PGL_2 action, no Mobius
transformation and no automorphism of P1 anywhere.

OBLIGATION. (i) The GL_2(k) action on Proj (k[X_0,X_1]) as a scheme automorphism — mathlib's
Proj functoriality for graded ring isomorphisms is the intended route; check what this exact
mathlib rev ships before hand-rolling. (ii) Transitivity on P^1(k), or the weaker form actually
needed: for any two distinct c_0, c_1 in P^1(k) an automorphism carrying them to [1:0], [0:1].
(iii) The compatibility hpi is preserved (gamma is over k), and fiberTwoCover (gamma . pi) is the
gamma-twisted two-chart cover.

ALTERNATIVE IF THIS IS TOO EXPENSIVE: repair R2 (generalize FinCoverData to sigma-charts, the
non-vanishing loci of theta sections). Wider refactor, stays inside the relThetaSections
vocabulary, owes affineness of the complement of an ample divisor. Do not attempt both.

######################################################################
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.swallow-adapt | pending
TITLE: Swallow-adapt: coarse chart-pair adaptation LANDED; chart-principality datum remains
HALF LANDED 2026-07-25 (run 0048, commit on Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean).

WHAT IS DONE. The coarse adaptation exists and its certificate obligations are discharged:
 * chartPairCoverData — a legal FinCoverData with m_0 = m_1 = 1, h = a = 1; the partition of unity
   is 1*1 = 1 and Scheme.basicOpen_one identifies each piece with its pinned chart
   (chartPairCoverData_pieces_inl / _inr / _eq);
 * DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair — builds the adaptation from a CHART-PRINCIPALITY datum via the
   landed anchored constructor DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors (DivisorFamily.lean:257): for each pinned
   chart, a member pt of d's cover with V_b <= d.cover.opens (pt), the chart equation, and the
   comparison unit;
 * forall_noLeak_of_pieces_eq_chart and forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart — for ANY
   adaptation whose pieces are the two pinned charts, a divisor with
   supportLocus subset V_0 cap V_1 is swallowed by every piece, so the assembler's hnoLeak and
   clause (c1)-finite hold. No fibre, no tube, no packet idempotent.
None of the landed no-gos touches this configuration: not_exists_unique_support_piece refutes ONE
support-meeting piece and this has TWO; supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated refutes
separation and this adaptation is maximally unseparated.

WHAT REMAINS: the CHART-PRINCIPALITY input, i.e. produce the (pt, eqn, unit) datum. It says the
divisor is cut by a single equation on each pinned chart. Route: a theta section psi in K has
exactly two chart components (relThetaResSide a b), so ONE psi supplies both equations at once;
div(psi) = d + E with E disjoint from the support, so psi cuts d on the open W = relCurve \ supp(E).
If W is not a whole chart, fall back to the FOUR-piece variant: a swallowing piece D(h_b) inside W
plus a complementary piece D(s_b) missing the support, obtained from comaximality of the disjoint
closed sets supportLocus and V_b \ W in the AFFINE V_b (sigma + tau = 1); the complementary piece's
equation is 1 and its colength VANISHES (subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus). The
pointwise gate licenses shrinking the base first, which is what makes a line bundle trivial on the
(semilocal after localization) divisor scheme spread to a Zariski neighbourhood.

GATED ON chart-avoid: without supportLocus subset V_0 cap V_1 the swallowing hypothesis is false.

AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyZarFunctor.lean:45:noncomputable def divFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
---
universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π] (n : ℕ)

/-- **The divisor functor** (DD-2 S6b, the pinned name): the locally certified
degree-`n` divisor families as a presheaf of types on the slice over `Spec k`,
with the glued restriction `divFamZar.map` along arbitrary test morphisms — the
`picDegLayerFunctor` house pattern. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
  obj T := divFamZar C π n T.unop
  map g := ↾divFamZar.map C π n g.unop
  map_id T := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T.unop => z.1 U) (divFamZar.map_id C π n s)
  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T''.unop => z.1 U)
      (divFamZar.map_comp C π n g.unop h.unop s)

@[simp]
lemma divFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
    (divFunctor C π n).obj T = divFamZar C π n T.unop :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma divFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
    (s : divFamZar C π n T.unop) :
    (divFunctor C π n).map g s = divFamZar.map C π n g.unop s :=
  rfl

end AlgebraicGeometry

THE ONE QUESTION THAT STILL NEEDS A HUMAN (2026-07-25, run 0048 r1). It is NOT "does the
Z(diamond) chart confine its divisors" — that is answered, NO (see chart-avoid). It is:

  OVER A SMALL FINITE FIELD, WHERE |P^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2, WHAT IS DivFamZar SUPPOSED TO BE?

WHY THE QUESTION IS FORCED. Certifiability requires the support to sit inside the preimages of a
pinned PAIR of points of P^1 (chart-avoid + confine-open). Every repair therefore needs, at every
base point, two k-rational points of P^1 off pi(supp_s) — i.e. q + 1 >= n + 2. And the
counterexample that kills chart-avoidance is FIELD-INDEPENDENT: F = s X_0^2 + X_0 X_1 + s X_1^2
is irreducible over F_2 exactly as over Q, because s(x^2+1) + x is degree 1 in s with coprime
coefficients over any field. So enlarging the field is not an escape and small fields are a real
hole, not a footnote.

WHAT MAKES IT A HUMAN DECISION. Challenge.lean:96-99 states the Jacobian over an ARBITRARY field,
and there is no hypothesis on k stronger than [Field k] anywhere in Picard/ or RiemannRoch/ (510
occurrences of Field k; zero Infinite / IsAlgClosed / PerfectField). The three options are not
comparable on mathematical grounds alone:

/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
consumes. -/
noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/

/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

end AlgebraicGeometry

    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)

namespace DivRepAffinePullback

/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
noncomputable def equiv
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
  toFun := D.pull S
  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
  left_inv v :=
    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
  right_inv := D.pull_classify S

@[simp]
theorem equiv_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem equiv_symm_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
  rfl

/-- Naturality of the assembled affine equivalence, in the frozen DDR-9 spelling. -/
theorem equiv_naturality
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)

=== 230,300 ===
/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
    (e : C ≅ C') :
    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op

/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
  sorry

/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/

/-- Identity coherence. -/
theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    baseChangeIso k k C =
      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
  sorry

/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    baseChangeIso k M C
        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
  sorry

/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/

variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]

theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
  sorry

end Jacobian

end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusOpen
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusFibreField
8	
9	/-!
10	# `chartLocus`: the class-indexed chart locus and its openness (C9a)
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean` proves openness of the witness locus of a *chosen*
13	basic-open cocycle datum `D`, and `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean` proves that the
14	witness predicate is intrinsic to the *fibre class* of the datum.  Neither file defines
15	`chartLocus` — until this one, the name occurred only in doc comments across the tree
16	(one of which, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:20`, calls it "the still-undefined
17	`chartLocus`").
18	
19	This file defines it, at the carrier level the consumers need — a locus in the parameter
20	space `Spec B`, indexed by a **class**, not by a datum — and proves the two facts the C9
21	consumers ask for:
22	
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocus` — `{q | every datum with fibre class `c` has a witness
24	  divisor with vanishing `H¹` at `κ(q)`}`.  A datum-choice-free predicate on
25	  `PrimeSpectrum B`.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_iff_exists` — the ∀-form and the ∃-form agree: since
27	  the witness predicate is class-intrinsic, quantifying over all data representing `c`
28	  and over some datum representing `c` give the same locus.  (Every class IS represented,
29	  by `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`.)
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus` — **the openness**, reduced to
31	  `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` at any one
32	  representing datum.
33	
34	Everything here is free of the DD-R certificate lane and of `divRep`: no
35	`DivFamZar`, no `IsCertified`, no `RepresentableBy` datum appears.  What is *not* here
36	is the C9 deliverable `f_c` (the chart morphism), which is genuinely gated on a
37	universal family; see the roadmap row `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus`.
38	-/
39	
40	set_option autoImplicit false
41	
42	universe u
43	
44	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
45	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
46	
47	open scoped TensorProduct
48	
49	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
50	
51	open AlgebraicJacobian
52	
53	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
54	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
55	
56	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
57	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
58	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
59	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
60	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
61	
62	variable (π) in
63	/-- **The chart locus of a class** (C9, `w4-datc` §3.3): the set of points of the
64	parameter space `Spec B` at which the fibre of the class `c` admits an effective witness
65	divisor with vanishing `H¹` — i.e. at which `c` is "seen by the chart".
66	
67	Stated over *classes*, not over data: a basic-open cocycle datum is a presentation, and
68	the campaign's consumers (dat-b B-6, dat-glue) index charts by the Picard class.  The
69	quantifier is harmless because the predicate is class-intrinsic
70	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`) and every class
71	is presented (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) — see
72	`mem_chartLocus_iff_exists`. -/
73	def chartLocus (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : Set (PrimeSpectrum B) :=
74	  {q : PrimeSpectrum B | ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
75	    D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField}
76	
77	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
78	    q ∈ chartLocus π c ↔ ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
79	      D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
80	  Iff.rfl
81	
82	/-- **Membership is testable at any one presentation**: a datum `D` presenting `c` is a
83	sound and complete test for membership of the chart locus.  This is the class-intrinsicity
84	of the witness predicate, `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, in the form
85	the consumers use. -/
86	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_of_datum {c : (relCurve C B).CechPic}
87	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hD : D.cechPicClass = c) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
88	    q ∈ chartLocus π c ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
89	  refine ⟨fun h => h D hD, fun h D' hD' => ?_⟩
90	  refine (D'.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq D
91	    q.asIdeal.ResidueField ?_).mpr h
92	  exact congrArg (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
93	    (hD'.trans hD.symm)
94	
95	/-- **The ∀-form and the ∃-form of the chart locus agree**: every class is presented by
96	some datum, and the witness predicate does not depend on which. -/
97	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_exists (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
98	    q ∈ chartLocus π c ↔ ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
99	      D.cechPicClass = c ∧ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
100	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
101	  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨D₀, hD₀, h D₀ hD₀⟩, fun ⟨D, hD, h⟩ => ?_⟩
102	  exact (mem_chartLocus_iff_of_datum D hD q).mpr h
103	
104	/-- **The chart locus is open** (C9a, the keystone the consumers cite): the class-indexed
105	locus is the witness locus of any one presenting datum, and that is open by
106	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` (the audited,
107	Noetherian-free openness engine).
108	
109	This is the first *datum-choice-free* openness statement of the C9 row — the earlier
110	engine output is stated for a chosen `D`, which is not what a chart indexed by a Picard
111	class may depend on. -/
112	theorem isOpen_chartLocus (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
113	    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : IsOpen (chartLocus π c) := by
114	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
115	  have hset : chartLocus π c
116	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
117	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
118	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
119	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
120	                    D₀.cechPicClass
121	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
122	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
123	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} :=
124	    Set.ext fun q => mem_chartLocus_iff_of_datum D₀ hD₀ q
125	  rw [hset]
126	  exact D₀.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
127	
128	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.AbelElement
8	
9	/-!
10	# The datum-level Abel–Jacobi map and its pointing law (Wave 6, `ofCurve`/`comp_ofCurve`)
11	
12	`Picard/AbelElement.lean` builds the Abel element `abelElement C P : pic0Subgroup C C` and
13	proves the pointing law `abelElement_map_point`.  `Picard/JacobianData.lean` pins the
14	representability datum with its universal property `homEquiv : (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`.
15	This file is the one-line bridge between them that the frozen Wave-6 gates consume:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map `C ⟶ d.J` of a rational
18	  point, `d.homEquiv.symm (abelElement C P)`.  The frozen `Jacobian.ofCurve`
19	  (`Challenge.lean:125`) is `(jacobianData C).ofCurve P` on the nose, since
20	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv_one` — the universal property sends the unit
22	  section to the trivial class.  This is *not* free: `η[d.J]` is `MonObj.one` of
23	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, which mathlib defines as `α.homEquiv'.symm 1`; the content
24	  is that `RepresentableBy.homEquiv'` (`ConcreteCategory/Representable.lean`) is
25	  `homEquiv` itself, so the two cancel.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.comp_ofCurve` — **the pointing law**
27	  `P ≫ d.ofCurve P = η[d.J]`, the datum-level avatar of the frozen
28	  `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve` (`Challenge.lean:130`).  Proved by injectivity of `homEquiv`,
29	  its naturality `homEquiv_comp` against `pic0Map`, and `abelElement_map_point`.
30	
31	Nothing here assumes a producer for `jacobianData`; everything is stated for an arbitrary
32	`d : JacobianData C`, in the section-variable discipline `JacobianData.lean` fixes.  The
33	universal-property half of Wave 6 (`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`, `Challenge.lean:141`) is
34	NOT addressed here and has no avatar anywhere.
35	-/
36	
37	set_option autoImplicit false
38	
39	universe u
40	
41	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
42	
43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
44	
45	namespace JacobianData
46	
47	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
48	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
49	
50	/-- **The datum-level Abel–Jacobi map** (design §4.6; the frozen `Jacobian.ofCurve`,
51	`Challenge.lean:125`): the morphism `C ⟶ d.J` classifying the Abel element of the
52	rational point `P`.  Already used unnamed at
53	`Picard/JacobianDataBaseChangeAbel.lean:115`; naming it is what makes the frozen gate a
54	one-liner. -/
55	noncomputable def ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
56	    C ⟶ d.J :=
57	  d.homEquiv.symm (abelElement C P)
58	
59	@[simp]
60	theorem homEquiv_ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
61	    d.homEquiv (d.ofCurve P) = abelElement C P :=
62	  d.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _
63	
64	/-- **The universal property sends the unit section to the trivial class**: the group
65	structure `d.grpObj` is `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, whose `one` is by definition
66	`d.rep.homEquiv'.symm 1`, and `RepresentableBy.homEquiv'` IS `homEquiv` — so the two
67	cancel by `Equiv.apply_symm_apply`. -/
68	theorem homEquiv_one (d : JacobianData C) :
69	    letI := d.grpObj
70	    d.homEquiv (η[d.J]) = 1 :=
71	  d.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply 1
72	
73	/-- **The pointing law** (the frozen `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve`, `Challenge.lean:130`): the
74	Abel–Jacobi map of `P` sends `P` itself to the neutral element of the group scheme
75	`d.J`.  Injectivity of the universal property reduces it to the naturality square
76	`homEquiv (P ≫ f) = pic0Map C P (homEquiv f)` and the landed pointing law
77	`abelElement_map_point`. -/
78	theorem comp_ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
79	    letI := d.grpObj
80	    P ≫ d.ofCurve P = η[d.J] := by
81	  letI := d.grpObj
82	  refine d.homEquiv.injective ?_
83	  rw [d.homEquiv_comp P (d.ofCurve P), homEquiv_ofCurve, homEquiv_one]
84	  exact abelElement_map_point P
85	
86	end JacobianData
87	
88	end AlgebraicGeometry

the locally certified quotient.  This is the choice-free per-chart operation from which
F5's affine forward map is glued. -/

    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) : DivFamZar C S pi g :=
  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar

TITLE: Chart-avoid: ANSWERED — NO. The Z(diamond) chart does not confine its divisors; the binding constraint is FinCoverData
ANSWERED 2026-07-25 (run 0048 round 1). The answer is NO, on three independent grounds, and
nothing downstream is blocked on a human any more. Deliverable of record: informal/spec-dd-r.md
ADDENDUM 3, which supersedes ADDENDUM 2 §4 and ADDENDUM 1 item 2. Inbox I-0333 is answered.

(a) THE SEED CARRIES NO EXACTNESS DATUM. ThetaGeneratorSeed (Picard/DivSchemeFamily.lean:74)
has five fields, IsGenerator (:129) two; none mentions Theta, pole order or a chart. Every
universal instantiation of `side` picks an ARBITRARY chart containing the point (seedUniv
DivSchemeSeedUnivGen.lean:283, seedUniv' DivSchemeRedesignSeedUniv.lean:180, pointwiseSide
DivSchemeSeedUnivPointwise.lean:88), so a point of pi^-1(infinity) is legal everywhere.

(b) ADDENDUM 2 §4's "tractable half" IS A WHOLE DISJUNCT, AND ITS ARGUMENT IS CIRCULAR. Theta =
fiberWeilDivisor pi is supported on V_0 \ V_1 (FLVFiberToolkit.lean:292/:311/:254), so
set-theoretically Theta = V_1^c and "supportLocus cap pi^-1(infinity) = empty" IS the disjunct
supportLocus subset V_1. And IsGenerator.dvd makes supportLocus the base locus of K, so "a
generator of exact pole order a exists at y in Theta" holds iff the base locus misses y:
premise = conclusion.

(c) EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE, STABLE UNDER EVERY ZARISKI SHRINK. Over k[t] with C = P^1, pi = id,
F = t X^2 + X Y + t Y^2 cuts a relative effective Cartier divisor, finite flat of degree 2
(coefficients (t,1,t) generate the unit ideal). F(1,0) = F(0,1) = t, so the fibre at t = 0 is
Z(XY) = {0, infinity}: it meets BOTH vertical fibres. In the chart Y = 1, F = t(x^2+1) + x is
degree 1 in t with coprime coefficients, hence irreducible in k[x,t]; the only point over Y = 0
is (infinity, 0), in the closure. So D is IRREDUCIBLE, D -> A^1_t is finite surjective, and over
EVERY nonempty open of the base D stays irreducible hence preconnected. Every Zariski cover has
a member containing t = 0. By supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified this divisor is NOT
IsLocallyCertified.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: the witness this leaf previously cited, Spec R[x]/(x^2 - t) over k[t],
does NOT meet pi^-1(infinity) (its points x = +-sqrt t are always finite), so it is chart-confined
and is not a witness. The conclusion stands; the witness above is the correct one.

(d) THE OBSTRUCTION SURVIVES THE DivEq QUOTIENT (landed this round, kernel-checked,
Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean): DivEq.supportLocus_eq — the support locus is a divisor
invariant — hence not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses: NO representative of
the class admits a certified adaptation. DivFamZar is a DivEq quotient, so DivFamZar is not the
relative-divisor functor and divRep against it would represent the wrong object.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT is FinCoverData (DivisorFamily.lean:160-176), which hardwires
h_0 : Fin m_0 -> Gamma(V_0), h_1 : Fin m_1 -> Gamma(V_1) with a partition of unity on EACH pinned
chart. Not pi, not the cover's fineness, not the submodule L, not the base. Any repair must
introduce an adaptation piece NOT contained in a single pinned chart. Successor leaves: p1-aut,
fibre-avoid, cert-relocalize, confine-open.

TITLE: Fibre-avoid: every relative divisor avoids two k-points of P^1 Zariski-locally on the base
THE COVERING OBLIGATION — what makes the atlas carve legitimate rather than lossy
(spec-dd-r ADDENDUM 3 §5). With p1-aut, this closes the certificate lane's geometric gate.

STATEMENT. For a relative divisor whose support is finite over Spec R, and any s in Spec R: the
fibre D_s is finite, so pi(D_s) is a finite subset of P^1 over kappa(s); if k is INFINITE then
P^1(k) is infinite, so two distinct c_0, c_1 in P^1(k) avoid pi(D_s). relCurve C R -> Spec R is
proper (instIsProperRelCurveHom, SupportTube.lean:194) hence closed, so the image of
supportLocus cap pi^-1({c_0,c_1}) is closed and misses s. Over the open complement the divisor is
confined to pi^-1(P^1 \ {c_0,c_1}) = V_0 inf V_1 for the gamma-twist carrying {c_0,c_1} to
{0,infinity}.

PAYOFF, ALREADY LANDED: chartPairCoverData / ofChartPair and
forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean) then give
clause (c1) FREE — no fibre, no tube, no packet idempotent. The base-open spread it needs is
confine-open's exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter.

 (i) k INFINITE. Challenge.lean states the Jacobian over an arbitrary field. A finite-field route
     needs |P^1(k)| > deg D, i.e. a base change to k(T) or a degree-d point; schedule it, do not

TITLE: Field-size: over a small finite field, what is DivFamZar? — the one remaining human decision
THE ONE QUESTION THAT STILL NEEDS A HUMAN (2026-07-25, run 0048 r1). It is NOT "does the
Z(diamond) chart confine its divisors" — that is answered, NO (see chart-avoid). It is:

  OVER A SMALL FINITE FIELD, WHERE |P^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2, WHAT IS DivFamZar SUPPOSED TO BE?

WHY THE QUESTION IS FORCED. Certifiability requires the support to sit inside the preimages of a
pinned PAIR of points of P^1 (chart-avoid + confine-open). Every repair therefore needs, at every
base point, two k-rational points of P^1 off pi(supp_s) — i.e. q + 1 >= n + 2. And the
counterexample that kills chart-avoidance is FIELD-INDEPENDENT: F = s X_0^2 + X_0 X_1 + s X_1^2
is irreducible over F_2 exactly as over Q, because s(x^2+1) + x is degree 1 in s with coprime
coefficients over any field. So enlarging the field is not an escape and small fields are a real
hole, not a footnote.

WHAT MAKES IT A HUMAN DECISION. Challenge.lean:96-99 states the Jacobian over an ARBITRARY field,
and there is no hypothesis on k stronger than [Field k] anywhere in Picard/ or RiemannRoch/ (510
occurrences of Field k; zero Infinite / IsAlgClosed / PerfectField). The three options are not
comparable on mathematical grounds alone:
 (a) accept |P^1(k)| >= n + 2 as a hypothesis, and RECORD that Challenge.lean:96-99 is then
     unreachable for small q — i.e. the challenge as stated is not solved;
 (b) plan a descent lane: divQProj (Picard/DivSchemeQProj.lean) is the right lever for fpqc
     descent from k'/k, so the Jacobian over k is obtained by descending from a big enough k';
 (c) generalize the pinned charts from k-rational points to closed points of degree d >= 2. This
     costs the two facts the whole design rests on — Gamma(P1 k, chartOpen k i) iso Polynomial k
     (Curve/P1Charts.lean:234,239) and isPrincipalIdealRing_chartSections (Curve/P1Points.lean:64)
     — because Cl(P^1 minus a degree-d point) = Z/d, not 0.

SETTLE THIS BEFORE p1-aut. It decides whether building the GL_2(k) action on P^1 is worth doing
at all: under (b) or (c) the twist may be unnecessary or insufficient.

REJECTED 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 2), on a source fact, before any Lean was written.

partitions of unity in FinCoverData to a JOINT covering drops the requirement from two
avoided points to ONE.  Worth trying before anyone builds PGL_2."

IT BUYS NOTHING, and the reason is a typing fact, not a proof attempt.  FinCoverData
(Picard/DivisorFamily.lean:160-176) types its pieces INTO the charts:
  h0 : Fin m0 -> Gamma(relCurve, V0)      (:166)
  h1 : Fin m1 -> Gamma(relCurve, V1)      (:168)
  pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen . h0) (basicOpen . h1)   (:186)
so every piece is a basic open OF ONE OF THE TWO PINNED CHARTS by construction, whatever
the partition data says.  Per-piece swallow-or-miss already holds for ANY cover by opens
(DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98 uses only openness of pieces), so a connected divisor still
lands in one piece, and basicOpen_le puts that piece inside one chart.  The joint-covering
relaxation changes the partition FIELDS; it cannot change where the pieces live.

SHARP FORM, which is what should be quoted from now on: no repair that keeps the pieces
inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P^1 can work.  Any real repair must
either vary the pinned pair (leaf p1-aut, the R1 route) or generalize FinCoverData's piece
TYPE away from the two charts (the recorded R2 alternative).

(w4-ddr9 §2.1 steps 1–2, assembled): a finite span-⊤ family `r : Fin m → S` such

theorem DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π g) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (r : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range r) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ p : Fin m,
        ∃ (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (r p)) π g)
          (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
          (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (r p)),
          (DivFam.mk G).toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlg (Localization.Away (r p)) g F₀ ∧
          (Module.Grassmannian.map w (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j)).toSubmodule
            = Submodule.map

                  b₁.equivFun.toLinearMap)
                (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mk G)).1 ∧

                  b₂.equivFun.toLinearMap)

9	/-!
10	# The datum-level Abel–Jacobi map and its pointing law (Wave 6, `ofCurve`/`comp_ofCurve`)
11	
12	`Picard/AbelElement.lean` builds the Abel element `abelElement C P : pic0Subgroup C C` and
13	proves the pointing law `abelElement_map_point`.  `Picard/JacobianData.lean` pins the
14	representability datum with its universal property `homEquiv : (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`.
15	This file is the one-line bridge between them that the frozen Wave-6 gates consume:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map `C ⟶ d.J` of a rational
18	  point, `d.homEquiv.symm (abelElement C P)`.  The frozen `Jacobian.ofCurve`
19	  (`Challenge.lean:125`) is `(jacobianData C).ofCurve P` on the nose, since
20	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv_one` — the universal property sends the unit
22	  section to the trivial class.  This is *not* free: `η[d.J]` is `MonObj.one` of
23	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, which mathlib defines as `α.homEquiv'.symm 1`; the content
24	  is that `RepresentableBy.homEquiv'` (`ConcreteCategory/Representable.lean`) is
25	  `homEquiv` itself, so the two cancel.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.comp_ofCurve` — **the pointing law**
27	  `P ≫ d.ofCurve P = η[d.J]`, the datum-level avatar of the frozen
28	  `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve` (`Challenge.lean:130`).  Proved by injectivity of `homEquiv`,
29	  its naturality `homEquiv_comp` against `pic0Map`, and `abelElement_map_point`.
30	
31	Nothing here assumes a producer for `jacobianData`; everything is stated for an arbitrary
32	`d : JacobianData C`, in the section-variable discipline `JacobianData.lean` fixes.  The
33	universal-property half of Wave 6 (`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`, `Challenge.lean:141`) is
34	NOT addressed here and has no avatar anywhere.
35	-/
36	
37	set_option autoImplicit false
38	
39	universe u
40	
41	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
42	
43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
44	
45	namespace JacobianData
46	
47	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
48	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
49	
50	/-- **The datum-level Abel–Jacobi map** (design §4.6; the frozen `Jacobian.ofCurve`,
51	`Challenge.lean:125`): the morphism `C ⟶ d.J` classifying the Abel element of the
52	rational point `P`.  Already used unnamed at
53	`Picard/JacobianDataBaseChangeAbel.lean:115`; naming it is what makes the frozen gate a
54	one-liner. -/
55	noncomputable def ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
56	    C ⟶ d.J :=
57	  d.homEquiv.symm (abelElement C P)
58	
59	@[simp]
60	theorem homEquiv_ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
61	    d.homEquiv (d.ofCurve P) = abelElement C P :=
62	  d.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _
63	
64	/-- **The universal property sends the unit section to the trivial class**: the group
65	structure `d.grpObj` is `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, whose `one` is by definition
66	`d.rep.homEquiv'.symm 1`, and `RepresentableBy.homEquiv'` IS `homEquiv` — so the two
67	cancel by `Equiv.apply_symm_apply`. -/
68	theorem homEquiv_one (d : JacobianData C) :
69	    letI := d.grpObj
70	    d.homEquiv (η[d.J]) = 1 :=
71	  d.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply 1
72	
73	/-- **The pointing law** (the frozen `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve`, `Challenge.lean:130`): the
74	Abel–Jacobi map of `P` sends `P` itself to the neutral element of the group scheme
75	`d.J`.  Injectivity of the universal property reduces it to the naturality square
76	`homEquiv (P ≫ f) = pic0Map C P (homEquiv f)` and the landed pointing law
77	`abelElement_map_point`. -/
78	theorem comp_ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
79	    letI := d.grpObj
80	    P ≫ d.ofCurve P = η[d.J] := by
81	  letI := d.grpObj
82	  refine d.homEquiv.injective ?_
83	  rw [d.homEquiv_comp P (d.ofCurve P), homEquiv_ofCurve, homEquiv_one]
84	  exact abelElement_map_point P

/-- **The pinned `functor.map` construction** (W7-F6, probe C): the morphism of group
objects `Grp.mk dY.J ⟶ Grp.mk dX.J` induced by a curve morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` —
contravariantly, pullback of degree-zero line-bundle classes.  The `yonedaGrp`-conjugate
of the degree-zero pullback transformation `pic0PullbackNat g` by the two representing
isomorphisms; the `IsMonHom` obligation is discharged by construction. -/
def pullbackHom (dX : JacobianData X) (dY : JacobianData Y) (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    letI := dX.grpObj
    letI := dY.grpObj
    (Grp.mk dY.J ⟶ Grp.mk dX.J) :=
  letI := dX.grpObj
  letI := dY.grpObj
  yonedaGrpFullyFaithful.preimage
    ((yonedaGrpObjIsoOfRepresentableBy dY.J _ dY.rep).hom
      ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (pic0PullbackNat g) (forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
      ≫ (yonedaGrpObjIsoOfRepresentableBy dX.J _ dX.rep).inv)

/-- **The defining equation of `pullbackHom`** (`map_preimage`): its `yonedaGrp` image
is the conjugated degree-zero pullback transformation.  Everything about `pullbackHom`
is proved through this equation and `yonedaGrp` faithfulness. -/
theorem yonedaGrp_map_pullbackHom (dX : JacobianData X) (dY : JacobianData Y)
    (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    letI := dX.grpObj
    letI := dY.grpObj
    yonedaGrp.map (pullbackHom dX dY g)
      = (yonedaGrpObjIsoOfRepresentableBy dY.J _ dY.rep).hom
        ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (pic0PullbackNat g) (forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
        ≫ (yonedaGrpObjIsoOfRepresentableBy dX.J _ dX.rep).inv :=
  yonedaGrpFullyFaithful.map_preimage _

/-- **`map_id` at the datum level** (ratified D1 shape: the datum argument is repeated
at the shared curve, so the frozen `functor.map_id` discharge is pure instantiation):
pullback along the identity curve morphism is the identity of `Grp.mk dX.J`.  By
`yonedaGrp` faithfulness from `pic0PullbackNat_id`. -/
theorem pullbackHom_id (dX : JacobianData X) :
    letI := dX.grpObj
    pullbackHom dX dX (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (Grp.mk dX.J) := by
  letI := dX.grpObj
  refine yonedaGrpFullyFaithful.map_injective ?_
  -- the conjugate collapses at the `yonedaGrpObj` level, where every composition is
=== baseChangeIsoOfData ===
    (fun {T} g => rfl)

/-- **W7-B6b — the datum-level base-change isomorphism**: for any two Jacobian data `d` on `C` and
`dL` on `C_L = (baseChange k L).obj C`, the base-changed group scheme
`(baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (Grp.mk d.J)` is isomorphic, as a group object over `L`, to
`Grp.mk dL.J`.  B-6a rewrites the `mapGrp` group structure to the transported datum's (via
`eqToIso`), and `Grp.mkIso` on the representing-object isomorphism
`(d.baseChange L).uniqueUpToIso dL` closes it, its `one`/`mul` compatibilities supplied by the
seam lemma
`isMonHom_hom_of_representableBy` fed with `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom`.  This is the datum-level
input consumed (definitionally, since `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`) by the frozen
`AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangeIso`. -/
noncomputable def baseChangeIsoOfData (d : JacobianData C) {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (dL : JacobianData ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C)) :
    letI := d.grpObj
    letI := dL.grpObj
    (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk d.J) ≅ .mk dL.J :=
  letI := d.grpObj
  letI := dL.grpObj
  letI := (d.baseChange L).grpObj
  haveI him :
      letI := MonObj.ofRepresentableBy (d.baseChange L).J
        ((pic0Functor ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C) ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
          ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat) (d.baseChange L).rep
      letI := MonObj.ofRepresentableBy dL.J
        ((pic0Functor ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C) ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
          ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat) dL.rep
      IsMonHom ((d.baseChange L).uniqueUpToIso dL).hom :=
    isMonHom_hom_of_representableBy
      ((pic0Functor ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C) ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
        ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat)
      (d.baseChange L).rep dL.rep ((d.baseChange L).uniqueUpToIso dL)
      (JacobianData.homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d.baseChange L) dL)
  eqToIso (congrArg
      (fun gg => ({ X := (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj d.J, grp := gg } :
        Grp (Over (Spec (.of L)))))

theorem one_le_windowδ : 1 ≤ windowδ π := one_le_classDeg_fiberTwist_one π

/-- `0 ≤ δ`. -/
theorem windowδ_nonneg : 0 ≤ windowδ π := le_trans zero_le_one (one_le_windowδ π)

/-- The fiber Weil divisor has degree `δ`: `deg F = δ` (DAT-0b,
`classDeg_fiberTwist_one`). -/
theorem deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ :
    CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) = windowδ π :=
  (classDeg_fiberTwist_one π).symm

/-! ## The multiplier step `s` and the embedding exponent `M` -/

private theorem windowS_exists (g : ℕ) :
    ∃ s : ℕ, windowBound π hπ + 3 * (g : ℤ) ≤ ((s : ℤ) - 1) * windowδ π := by
  set T : ℤ := windowBound π hπ + 3 * (g : ℤ) with hT
  refine ⟨T.toNat + 1, ?_⟩
  have hδ : 1 ≤ windowδ π := one_le_windowδ π
  have h1 : ((T.toNat : ℤ)) ≤ (T.toNat : ℤ) * windowδ π :=
    le_mul_of_one_le_right (Int.natCast_nonneg _) hδ
  have h2 : T ≤ (T.toNat : ℤ) := Int.self_le_toNat T
  have h3 : (((T.toNat + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) - 1) = (T.toNat : ℤ) := by push_cast; ring
  rw [h3]; linarith

/-- **The multiplier step `s`** — least `s` with `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 3g` (worksheet §2.1,
budget strengthened `2g → 3g` for the P-fib-N tower discharge at residue fields,
I-0234). Used by F3 (graded surjectivity of `H_s` onto the `P`-level algebra). -/
noncomputable def windowS_choice (g : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.find (windowS_exists π hπ g)

/-- **The strengthened defining inequality of `s`**: `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 3g` — the
P-fib-N tower budget `hβS` at `κ(p)` (I-0234). -/
theorem windowS_spec_three (g : ℕ) :
    windowBound π hπ + 3 * (g : ℤ) ≤ ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) - 1) * windowδ π :=
  Nat.find_spec (windowS_exists π hπ g)

/-- **The original defining inequality of `s`**: `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 2g` — kept in its
historical shape so every pre-I-0234 consumer is byte-compatible; strictly weaker than
`windowS_spec_three`. F3's `A_P`-surjectivity window. -/
theorem windowS_spec (g : ℕ) :
    windowBound π hπ + 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) - 1) * windowδ π := by
  have h := windowS_spec_three π hπ g
  have hg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (g : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _
  linarith

private theorem windowM_exists (g : ℕ) :
    ∃ M : ℕ, windowBound π hπ + 2 * (g : ℤ)
        + ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π
      ≤ (M : ℤ) * windowδ π := by
  set U : ℤ := windowBound π hπ + 2 * (g : ℤ)
      + ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π with hU
  refine ⟨U.toNat, ?_⟩
  have hδ : 1 ≤ windowδ π := one_le_windowδ π
  have h1 : ((U.toNat : ℤ)) ≤ (U.toNat : ℤ) * windowδ π :=
    le_mul_of_one_le_right (Int.natCast_nonneg _) hδ
  have h2 : U ≤ (U.toNat : ℤ) := Int.self_le_toNat U
  linarith

(worksheet §2.1). Chosen so every embedding/normalization/lane window down to depth
`g + 1` in `P`-steps stays `≥ b`. -/
